source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Record the date and time of the inspection as well as the vehicle identification number (VIN), make, model, and year of the vehicle being inspected.
3. Clearly state the purpose of the inspection and identify all inspectors involved by name and credentials.
4. Document the brake testing procedures used (e.g., deceleration tests, visual inspections, functionality tests) and any equipment utilized.
5. Detail the results of visual inspections, noting the condition of the brake pads, rotors, calipers, fluid levels, hydraulic lines, and other relevant components.
6. Clearly articulate the methodology used for measuring brake performance (e.g., pressure gauge readings, decelerometer readings, pedal feel).
7. Provide observations on the brake performance, including any noise, vibration, grabbing, fading, or pulling when the brakes are applied.
8. Specify the tests where the brakes failed to meet standards and provide measurement data (e.g., brake force below required percentage
